h:
Learning, culture and internal communications · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Store engagement drop alert

Gloria · Employee Experience Analyst

Seven resignations at the same store in the same month, and nobody saw it coming.

When it runs
Close of each biweekly pulse in the employee app, at 11:59 p.m. on Sunday, with processing on Monday at 6 a.m. and an alert to the regional HRBP at 8 a.m.
What it delivers in production
Every Monday by 8 a.m. the HRBP gets one alert per store in yellow or red, with the question that fell and the suggested action. The people director gets the chain's distribution by color.
Who decides
Classifies and alerts; the HRBP decides
Effort
Calibrate on 12 pulses; 3 supervised cycles
Set up5 steps · 8 ready files

# Climate radar thresholds (agreed with HR)

## Colors, by question, never by the average of the 4
- Red: drop of 0.6 point or more in p1 in 2 consecutive pulses, or average below 3.0 in any question.
- Yellow: drop of 0.6 point or more in 1 pulse, or average from 3.0 to 3.4 in any question.
- Green: none of the above.
- Average with 1 decimal place, rounded half up (2.625 becomes 2.6; 2.65 becomes 2.7). The drop uses the unrounded average.
- Minimum n: 8 respondents in the current pulse. Below that: BELOW MINIMUM N, no color, no average shown, no alert.
- Participation = responses ÷ headcount. Below 25% for 2 consecutive pulses: yellow, even with good averages.

## Context (does not cancel the alert)
- Manager change: manager_since up to 90 days before the pulse closing.
- Commercial event: end_date up to 15 days before the pulse closing. An event that has not happened yet is not context.

## Open alerts
- A store in open_alerts.csv that is still in alert: UPDATE, with the new color and the start pulse. It is not a new alert.
- A store in open_alerts.csv green in the previous pulse and in the current one: CLOSED.

## Who receives
- Yellow: the region's HRBP (hrbp column of stores.csv).
- Red: HRBP and case opening, both AWAITING APPROVAL from the culture coordinator.
- 3 or more reds in the same region in the same pulse: also the people director.
- Nothing goes to the store manager.

## Rules with no leeway
- The average of the 4 questions does not decide color. E.g.: 0472 has an overall average of 3.6, but p1 at 2.6 and two consecutive drops (4.1 to 3.4 to 2.6): red.
- A store with n below 8 does not appear in a block, table or sentence, only in the BELOW MINIMUM N count. E.g.: 0305, with 3 responses.
- Context: E.g.: 0472 with a manager since Sep 28 (48 days) and inventory count until Nov 8 (7 days before) are in; Black Friday on Nov 27 has not happened yet and is not in.
- optional_text is never quoted and no manager name appears. Write only the theme.
- Participation of 0472: 8 of 34 (23.5%) in this pulse, but 11 of 34 (32.4%) in the previous one: not 2 consecutive pulses.
- A store below the minimum n has no line of its own. E.g.: 0305 with 3 responses: the output brings only "BELOW MINIMUM N: 1"; the code 0305, the region and the n do not appear, not even to explain the exclusion.
- Do not prove the exclusion. Wrong: "Note: store 0305 (3 respondents) appears only in BELOW MINIMUM N" and, in the STATE, "0305 (n=3)". Right: only "BELOW MINIMUM N: 1" on the distribution line, with no note, and the same in the STATE.
- The final answer, the run report and the STATE are outputs too: what a rule says to omit does not appear in them, not even to explain the exclusion.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

A store's result goes to the HRBP, never to its manager: the question 'I trust my manager' answered by 9 people points fingers if it lands in the wrong hands. A store with fewer than 8 respondents gets no color or alert and only counts in the regional average. The optional text is read for theme and never quoted. The agent does not suggest warning, replacing or dismissing a manager: it suggests a conversation and checking the context. Red alerts and case opening wait for the culture coordinator at the Connector decisions gate, with no approval by timeout. The Radar works through an HR service account, read-only on the pulse Sheets and writing restricted to the alerts channel.

Common mistakes

  • Comparing the inventory week's pulse with the previous one without noting the event in the context; the drop is one-off fatigue and the alert becomes noise.
  • Using the average of the 4 questions as the store's single indicator; one question at 2.5 and three at 4.5 give a good average and hide the problem.
  • Reading a sudden drop in a store's participation as lack of interest, and not as fear of responding, which deserves the same alert.
  • Resetting the store's history when the manager changes; the new manager's first 2 pulses are the most useful data.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Lead time between the first alert and the store's resignation peakfrom zero (found out afterward) to 4 to 6 weeksestimate based on the described routine
Stores with a sustained drop identified before the high-turnover quarter70% or more, the calibration acceptance criterionestimate based on the described routine
Time between pulse close and alert to the HRBPfrom 2 to 4 weeks (monthly PDF) to under 9 hoursestimate based on the described routine
